title: Spectral Resonance Material Lab
description: A paleontology lab where a translucent skull and amber-encased mosquito sit on pedestals. The user manipulates material properties across both objects using a shared energy budget — increasing subsurface scattering on the skull drains energy available for the amber's refraction index, and vice versa. The goal is to tune both specimens to match a target spectral signature while respecting conservation of total material energy.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load ScatteringSkull.glb on the left pedestal and MosquitoInAmber.glb on the right pedestal. Use a dark museum-style environment with three colored spotlights (warm amber, cool blue, neutral white) illuminating the scene. Camera starts at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at origin. Implement a shared energy budget system with a total of 100 energy units. Create an HTML overlay panel with sliders controlling: (1) Skull subsurface scattering intensity 0-50, (2) Skull metalness 0-1, (3) Skull emissive glow color via hue slider 0-360, (4) Amber refraction distortion 0-50, (5) Amber opacity 0.1-1.0, (6) Amber emissive glow color via hue slider 0-360. Sliders 1 and 4 share the energy budget — their sum cannot exceed 100. When one increases, clamp the other automatically and flash a warning. Apply MeshPhysicalMaterial to both models with transmission, thickness, roughness, and ior properties mapped to slider values. Display a real-time energy bar showing budget allocation split between skull (blue) and amber (orange). Generate a random target configuration shown as small color swatches. Add an Undo button and Redo button that track all slider changes in a history stack supporting at least 15 states. Add a Reset button restoring defaults. Add a Score display that computes percentage match to the target across all six parameters. When score exceeds 90%, trigger a particle burst celebration effect using Points geometry. OrbitControls should allow full rotation. Each model should slowly rotate on its pedestal via animation loop. Ensure all materials update in real-time as sliders change.
